hardware: NVIDIA RTX A6000 48 GiB sm_86 (CUDA 12.9, driver 13.4/616.92, WSL2); Intel Core i9-13900K 32 logical CPUs; 32 GiB host; Warp 1.17.0; Python 3.12

suites.acceptance: For each species (p, He, C, O) and each qualified material: tabulated electronic stopping power within 1.5 % (p, He) / 3 % (C, O) of a held-out evaluation table (role 'evaluation', distinct from construction data) over the documented energy domain; Monte Carlo R80 in water within max(0.5 mm, 0.5 %) (p, He) / max(0.7 mm, 0.7 %) (C, O) of the CSDA range of the evaluation table with the same mean-excitation-energy lineage (ICRU 90, I = 78 eV, whose values above the blend window are held out from construction; for oxygen the effective-charge-scaled ICRU 90 lineage), at >= 1e5 histories per energy for >= 3 energies per species. PSTAR/ASTAR (ICRU 49, I = 75 eV) are reported as a second evaluation with their documented +0.5 % range offset; they are the same-lineage reference for non-water materials.
suites.rationale: Ion-specific stopping/range evidence is required per species; proton data cannot validate heavier ions (V2-ION, V2-EVID).
suites.independent_evidence: ion-specific-tabulated evaluation tables (PSTAR/ASTAR/ICRU 90 lineage) with construction/evaluation roles recorded

suites.acceptance: Pristine 70, 150, 230 MeV protons in water vs TOPAS (independent MC) at matched configuration: |dR80| <= 1.0 mm; distal 80-20 % width within 0.5 mm; central-axis depth-dose gamma (3 % local of maximum, 1 mm) pass rate >= 95 % over 0..R80+5 mm; lateral sigma at 3 depths within max(5 %, 0.2 mm). Additionally R80 within 1.5 mm of a non-Geant4 range reference (PSTAR/ASTAR CSDA or measured range data).
suites.rationale: Depth dose and lateral spread are the primary planning observables; evidence must be independent of the implementation.
suites.independent_evidence: independent Monte Carlo (TOPAS), measured/analytic Bragg-curve references

suites.acceptance: 150 and 230 MeV protons in water vs TOPAS: primary-proton fraction at R80-10 mm within 0.03 absolute; secondary-particle dose fraction within 30 % relative; plateau dose (20-50 mm) within 3 %; a discriminating run with nuclear physics disabled must change the plateau dose by >= 5 % and be reported as such.
suites.rationale: Nuclear attenuation and secondaries change the plateau by roughly 10-15% for 200 MeV protons; the model must be evidenced, not just enabled.
suites.independent_evidence: independent Monte Carlo (TOPAS), published cross-section evaluations

suites.acceptance: Slab phantoms (compact bone, lung, adipose inserts) and the explicit heterogeneous planning variant, 150 MeV protons and 290 MeV/u carbon, vs TOPAS: |dR80| <= 1.5 mm on axis; 3-D gamma (3 %, 2 mm) pass rate >= 95 % in voxels above 10 % of maximum; MCsquare and/or FRED results recorded as supporting evidence with their differences explained.
suites.rationale: Material/density handling is central to patient-like planning geometries.

suites.acceptance: Helium-4 at 100, 150, 220 MeV/u in water vs TOPAS: |dR80| <= 1.0 mm; depth-dose gamma (3 %, 1 mm) >= 95 %; lateral sigma within max(7 %, 0.3 mm); R80 within 0.5 % of the ASTAR-lineage CSDA range (ion-specific tabulated).

Carbon-12 at 150, 290, 400 MeV/u in water vs TOPAS (BIC or QMD, recorded): |dR80| <= 1.0 mm; peak-to-plateau ratio within 10 %; fragment-tail dose integrated over R80+10..R80+40 mm within 25 % relative; primary carbon fraction at R80-10 mm within 0.05 absolute; H+He share of tail dose within 30 %; if measured fragment-yield data are acquired (role evaluation), charge-resolved yields within 30 %.
suites.rationale: Carbon nuclear physics and fragment dose are central release requirements.
suites.independent_evidence: independent Monte Carlo (TOPAS/Geant4 QMD or BIC), measured fragment yields where accessible

suites.acceptance: Oxygen-16 at 200 and 400 MeV/u in water vs TOPAS: |dR80| <= 1.5 mm; peak-to-plateau within 12 %; tail dose (R80+10..R80+40 mm) within 30 %; supported domain 100-430 MeV/u documented; requests outside it raise errors.
suites.rationale: Oxygen needs a documented supported domain with ion-specific validation.
suites.independent_evidence: independent Monte Carlo (TOPAS), ion-specific tabulated stopping data

suites.acceptance: Dose-averaged LET on the central axis (unrestricted electronic stopping power in water, transported charged hadrons/ions) vs TOPAS scorer of the same definition: within 10 % proximal to R80-5 mm and 15 % in the peak/distal region, for 150 MeV protons and 290 MeV/u carbon (mixed field, species-resolved); entrance LET within 2 % of the analytic single-track value; undefined LET voxels reported as NaN.
suites.rationale: LET is a required planning observable and depends on estimator definitions.
suites.independent_evidence: independent Monte Carlo (TOPAS LET scorers), analytic limits

suites.acceptance: Predeclared bounds for 150 MeV protons and 290 MeV/u carbon in water at >= 1e5 histories: halving max step (1 -> 0.5 mm) and energy-step fraction (0.10 -> 0.05) changes R80 by <= 0.2 mm and peak dose by <= 1 %; shifting the scoring grid by half a voxel conserves integral dose to 0.1 % and R80 to 0.3 mm; translated/rotated sources and beam orientations reproduce profiles within statistics (|z| < 3, mean |z| < 0.2); float32 vs float64 total energy deposited within 0.01 % and voxel doses within statistics; finite-phantom escape and truncation energies are reported separately and the energy balance closes to 0.1 %; inapplicable probes are explained. Domains violating a bound are rejected and documented.
suites.rationale: Adversarial numerical falsification is a v2 MUST.

suites.acceptance: Batch-based uncertainty: 1-sigma interval coverage across >= 1000 high-dose voxels within 0.60-0.76 (nominal 0.683); relative uncertainty vs histories fits an exponent within -0.5 +/- 0.1 for dose, LET numerators and each fragment-species dose; identical seed and backend reproduce bitwise; different seeds give |mean z| < 0.1 and std z within 0.9-1.1; batch counts 2/10/40 recorded; undefined uncertainty is represented explicitly, never as zero.
suites.rationale: Undefined uncertainty must not masquerade as zero.

suites.acceptance: Reference Python (>= 2e4 histories), Warp CPU and Warp CUDA (>= 1e6) on identical configurations: total energy per primary within 0.1 % (and |z| < 3); voxelwise z-score distribution with |mean| < 0.1 and std within 0.9-1.15; CPU vs CUDA gamma (1 %, 1 mm) >= 99 %; deterministic repeat per backend and seed.
suites.rationale: Backends share the physics model; parity is equivalence, not accuracy evidence.

suites.acceptance: Every public path (simulate, dose, LET, influence, CLI) with all combinations of nuclear/secondaries/fragmentation/LET/species/biological/influence flags either honours the request with a discriminating observable change or raises an unsupported-combination error before any result; requested and effective configuration persisted and compared; supported species/materials/geometries/energies/sources/scorers/backends discoverable via API and documented. All tests pass.
suites.rationale: Fail-closed capability contract is a v2 MUST.

suites.acceptance: User-provided species/energy(/material) lookup tables (JSON/NumPy) accumulate tallies equal within statistics to the fluence-weighted expectation in controlled monoenergetic and mixed-field cases; the provenance (hash, source) is persisted; a table derived from the implementation's own stopping data is rejected as demonstration evidence. All tests pass.
suites.rationale: External biological lookup functionality must be demonstrated nontrivially.

suites.acceptance: A persisted result reopened in a separate clean process (no access to the producing objects) recovers every V2-OUTPUT field; influence matrices retain geometry, beamlet mapping, units, histories and normalization; human-readable summaries/profiles/plots are produced. All tests pass.
suites.rationale: Self-describing results are a release requirement.

suites.acceptance: External datasets are acquired through the provenance cache with URL, retrieval time, license/access basis, hash and role; cached reuse works offline; a hash mismatch fails; results identify the dataset hashes used. All tests pass.

Each performance.json workload measured on warp-cuda with all workload physics enabled and >= 10 batches satisfies every frozen target of decision 0039 (see performance_targets); warp-cpu and reference-path measurements and the scaling series are recorded; measurement method, concurrency and noise (>= 3 repeats) documented; failed runs retained.

From a fresh virtual environment, following only the documentation: install, acquire/cache data, define water, heterogeneous, multi-beamlet and carbon cases, run on the reference, warp-cpu and warp-cuda backends, obtain dose, LET, uncertainty and influence outputs, inspect human-readable results, and rerun offline from the cache. Any deviation is an acceptance failure.
suites.rationale: A product, not internal tests, is the deliverable.

suites.acceptance: pre-commit, CI (pre-commit, tests, docs) and the local exact-SHA validation gate pass; the qualification report covers all 53 MUST IDs with supporting suites; release promotion completes.

performance_metric_definitions: See decisions/0039: wall_seconds end-to-end warm-cache; histories_per_second = primaries / transport wall time (host+kernel, all batches); cold_start_seconds process start to first launch with warm kernel cache; compilation_seconds extra time of a run after warp.clear_kernel_cache(); host_seconds non-kernel transport time; gpu_kernel_seconds summed kernel time; peaks attributable device memory / host RSS.
amendment_policy: Any change requires a new decision record citing 0039, preserves this file's history and original results, records a tolerance_changed/validation_strategy_changed event, and re-freezes at a new SHA.

amendments.change: PHY-STOPPING-RANGE acceptance text clarifies which table is the same-lineage range reference (ICRU 90 for water); numeric tolerances and all other suites unchanged.
